name: Arduino Uno R4 Minima
summary: The Uno shape and 5 V logic, with a 48 MHz Renesas RA4M1 underneath: a real DAC, an op-amp, CAN, and 14-bit ADC.
notes: Still 5 V logic, which is the reason to pick this over almost any other modern board. Uno R3 shields and 5 V sensors work without level shifting, and IOREF is tied to 5 V to say so.
A0 is a real 12-bit DAC, not PWM with a filter. It is the only pin that can do it, and the first analog output on any Uno.
A1, A2 and A3 are the on-chip op-amp: plus input, minus input and output, in that order. Leave the op-amp disabled and they are ordinary analog inputs.

CAN is on D4 and D5, and the official datasheet gets this backwards in its description column. The pinout diagram's peripheral table is right: D4 is CTX0, the transmitter, and D5 is CRX0, the receiver. Either way you still need an external transceiver; these are logic-level pins.
Not every pin can raise an interrupt. The RA4M1 routes IRQ lines to D0, D1, D2, D3, D8, D12, D13, A4 and A5 only, which is a trap if you are porting code from a board where every pin could.
PWM is on D3, D5, D6, D9, D10 and D11, the same pins as the Uno R3.
A4 and A5 are the same silicon pins as D18 and D19, and they carry I2C. You get the analog input or the I2C bus, not both at once.
The ADC will do 14 bits if you ask for it with analogReadResolution. It defaults to 10 for compatibility with code written for the R3.
Position 1 on the power header is BOOT on this board, where the R3 had an unconnected pin. The barrel jack takes 6 to 24 V, a much wider range than the R3 was happy with.

pins.name: SCL
pins.note: Same silicon pin as A5, duplicated on the header for shields.

pins.name: AREF
pins.note: Only drive this after switching the reference in software.

pins.name: D13
pins.note: The LED pin. Not PWM capable, same as on the Uno R3.

pins.name: D5
pins.note: CAN receive, despite what the datasheet's description column says.

pins.name: D4
pins.note: CAN transmit. Needs an external transceiver to reach a bus.

pins.name: D0
pins.note: Receive, not transmit. The datasheet's pin table misprints this one as TX0.

pins.name: BOOT
pins.note: Where the R3 had an unconnected pin. It picks the boot mode at reset.

pins.name: IOREF
pins.note: Tied to 5 V. A shield reads this to find out what levels the board speaks.

pins.name: VIN
pins.note: Shared with the barrel jack, through a buck converter rather than a linear regulator.

pins.name: A0
pins.note: The only true analog output on the board.
